question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed 12-line or 700 UTF-16-unit default for collapsing existing users’ long chat prompts across web, iOS, and Android?
rationale: This is a new default user-visible transcript behavior rather than a repair to an established broken contract; the patch is technically bounded, but code review cannot choose the permanent UX threshold or accessibility trade-off.

options.title: Accept the shared disclosure default
options.body: Approve the 12-line or 700-unit rule as the cross-platform default and land after the refreshed required checks pass.

options.title: Adjust the product policy first
options.body: Ask for a different threshold, accessibility presentation, or scope before accepting the implementation.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the existing fully expanded transcript behavior until a broader chat readability decision is made.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared disclosure default
recommendation.body: Approve the 12-line or 700-unit rule as the cross-platform default and land after the refreshed required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies steipete as the author of the cross-platform proposal; a current-main feature-history trace was not available to identify a stronger UI owner.
